title: Unit testing with JUnit 5 and TestNG

videos.script: Lesson 6 ended with a constraint that compiled, sat on the record, and checked nothing. Nobody noticed, because nothing failed. {{unchecked}} A test is how you notice. It is a small program that calls your code with an input you chose. When the answer is wrong, it says so. {{test}} This lesson writes the bookshop's first tests. They need no server, no database and no Spring. Just the ISBN rule, a book's stock and an order's total. {{domain}} Maven runs them, and you learn to read what it prints: how many ran, which one failed, and where. {{surefire}} One test method can check many inputs, and each one is reported by name. {{parameterized}} Then you break the check digit on purpose. One test catches it. Take a single ISBN out of the list, and the broken rule goes through green. {{broken}} Nested classes and AssertJ make a test read like the thing it checks, and fail with a message worth reading. {{assertj}} Last, TestNG, the other framework. Its tests may depend on each other, and you will see what that buys and what it costs. And why Spring chose JUnit. {{testng}}
